_doc: ARTICLE SOURCES — lets the user switch where article/timeline/tone data comes from: the self-hosted GDELT proxy (data/topics.json's `api.base`) or a well-known public RSS/Atom feed fetched directly from the handset. Adding a source is an entry HERE plus a rebuild — no Kotlin change, same pattern as data/topics.json. Baked into BuildConfig.SOURCES_B64 by app/build.gradle. Every url below was verified reachable and item-counted by hand before being added; none are placeholders or guesses — do not add a source without doing the same.
_doc_fields: id: stable key, used as the persisted 'active source' value and (for non-query-driven rss sources) as the synthetic topic id its articles are filed under. label: shown in the UI source picker. kind: 'gdelt' (talks to api.base from topics.json, one query per topic) or 'rss' (parses an RSS2.0/RSS1.0(RDF)/Atom feed directly). url: rss only — the feed URL, with a literal '{query}' placeholder substituted (URL-encoded) for query_driven feeds. query_driven: true if the source takes a search term per topic (gdelt-self, google-news); false if it's one fixed feed regardless of topic (front page / section feeds) — those are fetched ONCE per refresh and filed under the synthetic topic id == source id, never once per topic. capabilities: subset of ['articles','timeline','tone'] this source can actually produce — no RSS source below carries a tone/sentiment field, so every rss entry lists only 'articles'; a UI must not offer timeline/tone charts for a source that doesn't declare that capability. requires_mesh: true only for gdelt-self, which needs the self-hosted proxy (public gateway or WireGuard mesh) to be reachable; every rss source is fetched straight from the public internet.
